    hover_data=["Hospital Type"],
    category_orders={"Death Stage": ["Early Neonatal (0-7d)", "Late Neonatal (8-28d)", "Postneonatal (29d-1y)"]},
    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Set3,
    stripmode="group"

fig.update_layout(
    title="Infant Death Counts by Region, Stage, and Hospital Type in Romania (2022)",
    xaxis_title="Region",
    yaxis_title="Death Stage",

SUMMARY
 This chart is a swarm plot illustrating infant death counts in Romania for the year 2022, segmented by region, death stage, and hospital type. The title of the chart, "Infant Death Counts by Region, Stage, and Hospital Type in Romania (2022)," clearly indicates its focus. The x-axis represents the different regions of Romania, including Bucharest-Ilfov, North-East, South-East, South-Muntenia, South-West Oltenia, West, North-West, and Center. The y-axis shows the death count, ranging from 10 to 70.

Each data point on the chart corresponds to a specific death count, color-coded to represent three distinct death stages: Early Neonatal (0-7 days), Late Neonatal (8-28 days), and Postneonatal (29 days to 1 year). The Early Neonatal stage is represented in a teal color, Late Neonatal in a yellow hue, and Postneonatal in a light blue shade. The points are grouped closely within each region, allowing for a comparison of death counts across different stages.

In the Bucharest-Ilfov region, the highest death counts are observed in the Early Neonatal stage, with values reaching 68 and 64. The Late Neonatal stage in this region shows death counts of 28 and 27, while the Postneonatal stage has a count of 38. In the North-East region, Early Neonatal deaths range from 48 to 55, Late Neonatal counts are between 19 and 22, and Postneonatal deaths stand at 28. The South-East region displays Early Neonatal death counts between 38 and 42, Late Neonatal counts of 15 and 18, and a Postneonatal count of 23.

The South-Muntenia region shows similar patterns with Early Neonatal deaths ranging from 44 to 50, Late Neonatal counts of 19 and 21, and a Postneonatal count of 28. The South-West Oltenia region has Early Neonatal counts between 30 and 35, Late Neonatal counts of 13 and 15, and a Postneonatal count of 19. In the West region, Early Neonatal deaths are 44 and 52, Late Neonatal counts are 18 and 20, and the Postneonatal count is 27.

The North-West region shows Early Neonatal death counts of 42 and 48, Late Neonatal counts of 17 and 19, and a Postneonatal count of 25. Lastly, the Center region has the highest Early Neonatal death counts, with values of 50 and 58, Late Neonatal counts between 19 and 24, and Postneonatal counts of 19 and 30. This detailed visualization allows for an in-depth understanding of the distribution and frequency of infant deaths across different stages and regions in Romania.
